title: Workspace Is Draft
prompt: A TypeScript workflow uses status strings for workspaces. Write a function that returns true only when status is "draft".

explanation.beginner:
Example: workspaceIsDraft("draft") produces true. The result must follow this precise rule: A TypeScript workflow uses status strings for workspaces. Write a function that returns true only when status is "draft". Work with one argument at a time and distinguish the values that select a branch from the values returned by that branch.

Compare “rejects published”: input ["published"] produces false. Explain which rule causes the difference before writing code.
explanation.junior:
The result must follow this precise rule: A TypeScript workflow uses status strings for workspaces. Write a function that returns true only when status is "draft". Work with one argument at a time and distinguish the values that select a branch from the values returned by that branch.

Tempting mistake: Do not hard-code the first example: the rejects published case changes the input contract’s boundary or shape. Compare the actual outputs rather than only checking whether both are truthy.

Trace the branch conditions and any accumulator or lookup after each input. Keep the return contract separate from how it is calculated.

Regression check: preserve the contract illustrated by “rejects published”, then change one boundary in a new test. The solution below is one implementation; another is valid when it preserves the same behavior.
